previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic intestinal dysmotility, and a long-standing femoral central venous catheter presented with fevers during an outpatient iron infusion. She was found to have a coagulase-negative staphylococcal bloodstream infection likely originating from her central line. Initial management included IV vancomycin and monitoring, but the catheter developed a mechanical leak despite a bedside repair. Due to ongoing infection risk and device failure, the catheter was replaced via interventional radiology. She received a full course of IV antibiotics, completed her iron infusion, and remained stable throughout. She was discharged home with plans for continued IV vancomycin, vancomycin-heparin locks, and home nursing support, with follow-up arranged.

Information for Outpatient Providers: ___ female with a

#Headache
#Migraine
Patient has history of migraines, with multiple previous 
hospitalizations for migraines, including 2 in ___. Usually 
responds to cocktail of Toradol+Reglan+Imitrex. This time
resistant to treatment received in the ED consisting of IV 
dilaudid/Metoclopramide/Ketorolac. Clinical picture strongly 
suggestive of her typical complex migraine headache, though now 
with L sided throbbing quality, usually R sided per patient. On 
___, had CTA with no aneurysm or evidence of new acute 
infarct. Also, no meningismus or fever so less concerning for 
infectious etiology. On ___, with concern of new onset 
expressive aphasia and left sided weakness for which a code 
stroke was called; symptoms had reportedly resolved en route to 
CT with NCHCT negative for acute infarction. Attempted Fiorcet 
for her migraine without improvement; migraine did spontaneously 
resolve over the ensuing days. She usually gets botox injections 
for her migraines and is due for follow-up with her specialist 
on ___. She did experience a re-emergence of aphasia and left 
lower extremity weakness on ___ for which neuro was 
re-consulted. Neurology felt that her symptoms in both episodes 
were more consistent with her complex partial migraine history 
and given that she failed her prior prophylactic regimen, she 
would benefit greatly from seeing her specialist on ___ for 
another botox injection. 

#Ileus. Patient with history of multiple SBOs and has G-tube for 
decompression. Follows with Dr. ___ as an outpatient in GI.

advanced which she tolerated without emesis though continued to
